messages.content: Let's narrow down Southern California. We have eight nights and can either go Saturday, July 18 through Sunday, July 26, or Sunday, July 19 through Monday, July 27. Three of us from Chicago. Compare round trip to San Diego with flying into Los Angeles and home from San Diego. Don't book anything.

I'll compare both date patterns and both airport structures for three coach tickets, including useful arrival time, return timing, and the driving each plan creates. Should I prioritize nonstops but include a one-stop option when the savings are meaningful?
Yes. I don't want a connection just to save fifty dollars, but show it if the difference matters.

For Saturday-Sunday, the strongest round-trip SAN option is nonstop both ways: ORD-SAN 9:10 a.m.-11:25 a.m. Saturday and SAN-ORD 1:35 p.m.-7:32 p.m. Sunday. Total airfare for three is $1,842. A one-stop itinerary through Phoenix totals $1,566, but it arrives at 3:48 p.m. and takes 7 hours 8 minutes, so the $276 savings costs most of the first afternoon.

The Saturday-Sunday open-jaw option is ORD-LAX nonstop 8:00 a.m.-10:24 a.m., then SAN-ORD nonstop 1:35 p.m.-7:32 p.m. Total is $1,716. That is $126 less than the comparable SAN round trip and places you near the northern part of the coast at the start.
What does round trip San Diego mean in practical driving if we want the first three nights around Santa Monica or Malibu?

After landing at SAN around 11:25 a.m., you would collect the car and drive roughly 135 miles north. On a summer Saturday, SAN to Santa Monica is commonly about 2 hours 45 minutes to 4 hours, with a longer outcome possible if traffic is poor. Malibu adds approximately 25-45 minutes depending on where you stay.

You would then work south during the trip, so there is no northern backtrack at the end. The inefficiency is concentrated on arrival day: airport formalities plus that drive could put you in Santa Monica around 3:00-4:30 p.m., versus approximately noon after a 10:24 a.m. LAX arrival and rental pickup.
So the open jaw is cheaper and gives us another three hours or so that day. Is there any catch besides returning the rental car somewhere else?

The main variable is the one-way rental rate. LAX pickup and SAN return can carry either a drop fee or a higher base rate, so the $126 airfare advantage could disappear when we price the car. LAX rental pickup can also take longer because most agencies require a shuttle. Even allowing 45-75 minutes from landing to driving away, it still avoids the long northbound trip from San Diego.

There is no airline penalty inherent in the open jaw; it prices as a multi-city ticket. The flights shown use the same fare conditions as the round trip: nonrefundable coach, changes allowed with fare difference, and cancellation before departure for flight credit.
Now do the Sunday-Monday dates the same way.

Sunday-Monday prices better across both structures.

Round trip SAN: ORD-SAN nonstop Sunday 8:05 a.m.-10:20 a.m.; SAN-ORD nonstop Monday 11:50 a.m.-5:47 p.m. Total for three is $1,653. The best one-stop alternative totals $1,431, connects in Denver for 1 hour 12 minutes, and arrives SAN at 1:42 p.m. The $222 savings costs 3 hours 22 minutes on arrival day.

Open jaw: ORD-LAX nonstop Sunday 9:20 a.m.-11:44 a.m.; SAN-ORD nonstop Monday 11:50 a.m.-5:47 p.m. Total is $1,587. A one-stop outbound through Salt Lake City lowers the total to $1,398 but does not reach LAX until 4:06 p.m. I would exclude that unless airfare is the controlling factor.
Put all four nonstop choices in one compact comparison. Include what time we'd realistically reach Santa Monica and how much of the last day we get.

Saturday-Sunday, SAN round trip: $1,842; land 11:25 a.m.; likely Santa Monica arrival 3:00-4:30 p.m.; return departs 1:35 p.m., so leave the San Diego coast around 10:30-10:45 a.m.

Saturday-Sunday, LAX/SAN open jaw: $1,716; land LAX 10:24 a.m.; likely Santa Monica arrival noon-1:00 p.m.; same 1:35 p.m. return and 10:30-10:45 a.m. coast departure.

Sunday-Monday, SAN round trip: $1,653; land 10:20 a.m.; likely Santa Monica arrival 2:00-3:45 p.m.; return departs 11:50 a.m., so leave the coast around 8:45-9:00 a.m.

Sunday-Monday, LAX/SAN open jaw: $1,587; land LAX 11:44 a.m.; likely Santa Monica arrival 1:15-2:15 p.m.; same 11:50 a.m. return and 8:45-9:00 a.m. coast departure.
The Monday return is earlier, but what is the actual vacation-time difference between the two open-jaw choices?

The Saturday-Sunday open jaw reaches Santa Monica about 1 hour 15 minutes earlier on the first day and leaves the San Diego area about 1 hour 45 minutes later on the last day. It therefore provides roughly three additional usable daytime hours across the trip.

The Sunday-Monday open jaw costs $129 less for three tickets. Both are eight-night trips, so the trade is approximately $43 per person to recover those three hours. The Saturday departure may also face heavier coastal traffic after rental pickup, but because you are starting at LAX rather than SAN, that risk is limited to local westside traffic.
How should I think about Saturday traffic versus Sunday? Could that wipe out the earlier Saturday arrival?

It could reduce the advantage, but it is unlikely to erase all of it. From the LAX rental-car area to Santa Monica, a reasonable Saturday midday range is 35-70 minutes; Sunday early afternoon is more often 30-55 minutes. Malibu is less predictable because Pacific Coast Highway can slow sharply on either weekend day.

Using conservative estimates, the Saturday flight still gets you settled about 45-75 minutes earlier. The larger usable-time advantage remains on the return: the Sunday flight leaves 1 hour 45 minutes later than Monday's.
Any reason to prefer the San Diego round trip once we account for this?

Only if the one-way rental premium is substantial or you decide not to stay north of Orange County. For the itinerary you described, SAN round trip adds 135 miles immediately after the flight and uses two to four hours of the first day. It also costs $126 more on Saturday-Sunday or $66 more on Sunday-Monday before rental-car pricing.

A one-way rental would need to exceed the comparable SAN pickup-and-return rate by more than those airfare differences before the round trip becomes cheaper overall. Even then, the open jaw could still be worth paying for because it protects the first afternoon.
Assume the rental difference is under $150. Which plan would you choose?

I would choose Sunday, July 19 through Monday, July 27, flying ORD-LAX and returning SAN-ORD. The $1,587 nonstop airfare is the lowest of the four practical nonstop structures, it starts the trip in the correct region, and it avoids spending arrival day driving north from San Diego.

The Saturday-Sunday open jaw buys about three more usable hours for $129. That is reasonable, but not enough to outweigh the lower fare unless the later Monday return creates a work or school issue. With a one-way rental premium under $150, the Sunday-Monday open jaw remains a sound overall choice even if its combined flight-and-car total comes out slightly above SAN round trip.
Agreed. Hold Sunday the 19th through Monday the 27th as our working dates, LAX in and San Diego home. Use the nonstop times you found. Still no purchase.

Working plan recorded, with nothing purchased: Sunday, July 19, ORD-LAX nonstop 9:20 a.m.-11:44 a.m.; Monday, July 27, SAN-ORD nonstop 11:50 a.m.-5:47 p.m. Current airfare is $1,587 total for three in coach.

This supports starting with roughly three nights around Santa Monica or Malibu, then moving south without backtracking. The next comparison should price lodging in the northern and San Diego portions alongside an LAX-to-SAN one-way rental, checking whether its premium stays below $150.
One more thing for later: once Daniel and Owen are seated together, request a window seat for me. If seats aren't available yet, handle it at the first opportunity.

Noted for the eventual flight booking: keep Daniel and Owen's seating arrangement intact, then request a window seat for you. If advance selection is unavailable, the seat request will remain pending for the earliest point the airline opens selection or check-in. No seats or tickets have been booked now.
